scenes.visual: Title card 'Mean and Spread' fades in over a cloth bag spilling GOLD and BLUE beads. COLOUR MAP, same in both films: GOLD bead/bar = one allele (the 'gold' allele); BLUE bead = the other allele; a WHITE TRIANGLE under the axis = the mean (average) allele frequency across replicates; a horizontal axis labelled 'frequency of gold' runs 0 to 1. Cream background, 16:9. Every number appears only as on-screen text. Beads and bags are simple cartoons; dot clouds and histograms are computed from a Wright-Fisher model and labelled 'computed'; anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: An allele is common on an island and rare on the mainland. Did something favour it there, or was it luck? Or did migrants bring it?
scenes.visual: Left: a small island with a lizard silhouette and a bar 'gold allele: common' (mostly GOLD). Right: mainland with bar 'gold allele: rare' (mostly BLUE). Three question tags pop up one by one as each cause is named: 'favoured?', 'luck?', 'migrants?'.
scenes.narration: An allele is common on an island and rare on the mainland. Did something favour it there, or was it luck? Or did migrants bring it?

scenes.tts: Picture one generation's gene pool as a bag of beads. Gold beads carry one allele, and blue beads carry the other. Half of them are gold.
scenes.visual: A cartoon bag of 20 beads, 10 GOLD and 10 BLUE, shakes gently. Label 'one generation's gene pool'. A dot appears on the 0-to-1 axis below at 0.5, labelled 'this bag'.
scenes.narration: Picture one generation's gene pool as a bag of beads. Gold beads carry one allele, and blue beads carry the other. Half of them are gold.

scenes.tts: To make the next generation, a hand draws beads at random, and puts each one back after noting its colour. A small draw is rarely a perfect copy of the bag. This one came out heavy on gold.
scenes.visual: A hand draws one bead, a bead of the same colour drops into a second bag labelled 'next generation', and the drawn bead goes back into the first bag; this repeats 20 times (sped up). Label '20 draws, each bead put back'. The new bag lands 13 GOLD, 7 BLUE. The dot on the axis slides from 0.5 to 0.65 as the count updates on screen '13 of 20 gold'.
scenes.narration: To make the next generation, a hand draws beads at random, and puts each one back after noting its colour. A small draw is rarely a perfect copy of the bag. This one came out heavy on gold.

scenes.tts: Nobody chose gold. The sample was just small. Change in allele frequency from chance sampling of parents is called genetic drift. It needs no difference in fitness.
scenes.visual: The hand fades. Caption card 'genetic drift = chance change in allele frequency from sampling parents'. A small badge 'no fitness difference needed' stamps on beside it.
scenes.narration: Nobody chose gold. The sample was just small. Change in allele frequency from chance sampling of parents is called genetic drift. It needs no difference in fitness.

scenes.tts: One bag tells you little. So run many bags side by side, all starting half gold. Each bag is a replicate population.
scenes.visual: Five bags in a row (drawn), each with 20 beads, half GOLD. Below, the axis now holds 40 dots stacked at 0.5 (one per replicate; computed runs, only five bags drawn). Label 'replicate populations: same start, same conditions'. The WHITE TRIANGLE appears under 0.5.
scenes.narration: One bag tells you little. So run many bags side by side, all starting half gold. Each bag is a replicate population.

scenes.tts: Generation after generation, each bag wanders on its own. Some climb and some fall. A few reach all gold or all blue, and then they stay there.
scenes.visual: A generation counter ticks 0 to 20 (computed Wright-Fisher, 2N = 20 copies, 40 replicates). The 40 dots jitter and spread outward along the axis; dots that reach 0 or 1 turn solid and stop moving, piling at the ends. Bags above flicker their bead mix to match.
scenes.narration: Generation after generation, each bag wanders on its own. Some climb and some fall. A few reach all gold or all blue, and then they stay there.

scenes.tts: Now watch the white triangle. It marks the average across all the bags. The bags spread apart, but the triangle stays close to where it started.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the WHITE TRIANGLE under the axis as the generations keep ticking; it wobbles only slightly around 0.5 while the dot cloud keeps widening. A faint bracket over the cloud labelled 'spread' grows wider.
scenes.narration: Now watch the white triangle. It marks the average across all the bags. The bags spread apart, but the triangle stays close to where it started.

scenes.tts: That is drift's signature across replicates. It spreads them apart without pushing their average. Chance favours no direction, so the triangle only wobbles.
scenes.visual: Split label appears: under the bracket 'spread: grows', under the triangle 'average: no push, small wobble'. Arrows up and down on individual dots.
scenes.narration: That is drift's signature across replicates. It spreads them apart without pushing their average. Chance favours no direction, so the triangle only wobbles.

scenes.tts: Now make every bag ten times bigger, and start again. The dots still spread, but far more slowly. Bigger pools scatter less.
scenes.visual: Reset to 40 dots at 0.5. The bags swell; on-screen label '2N = 200 copies' replaces '2N = 20 copies'. Counter ticks 0 to 20 again (computed); this cloud widens much less, overlaid on a faint ghost of the earlier wide cloud for comparison.
scenes.narration: Now make every bag ten times bigger, and start again. The dots still spread, but far more slowly. Bigger pools scatter less.

scenes.tts: What sets the scatter is not simply the number of animals you count. It is the effective population size: the size of an ideal population that drifts as fast.
scenes.caption: What sets the scatter is not simply the number of animals you count. It is the effective population size, Ne: the size of an ideal population that drifts as fast.
scenes.visual: A head-count tally 'animals counted' is crossed through lightly; beside it a card 'effective population size, Ne' with a small ideal bag icon. No numbers compared.
scenes.narration: What sets the scatter is not simply the number of animals you count. It is the effective population size, Ne: the size of an ideal population that drifts as fast.

scenes.tts: Back to small bags, all half gold. Now pour beads from outside into every bag, mostly blue ones. That is gene flow.
scenes.visual: Small bags again, 40 dots at 0.5. A jug labelled 'immigrants: mostly blue' tips the same small pour of BLUE-heavy beads into every bag at once.
scenes.narration: Back to small bags, all half gold. Now pour beads from outside into every bag, mostly blue ones. That is gene flow.

scenes.tts: Every bag started at one half and got the same pour. So every dot slides the same distance toward the immigrants. The triangle slides with them. Unlike drift, this happens the same way every time.
scenes.visual: All 40 dots and the WHITE TRIANGLE shift left together by the same distance, toward a marker 'immigrants' frequency' near 0.2. A small tag 'all bags started at 0.5; same pour' sits by the cloud. A label 'gene flow pushes the average' appears. The cloud's width stays about the same during the slide.
scenes.narration: Every bag started at one half and got the same pour. So every dot slides the same distance toward the immigrants. The triangle slides with them. Unlike drift, this happens the same way every time.

scenes.tts: Last, let gold carriers leave slightly more offspring, in every bag. That is consistent selection. What happens to the triangle? And what happens to the spread?
scenes.visual: Reset to 40 dots at 0.5. Gold beads gain a tiny glow in every bag and the hand's draw is tilted slightly toward them; label 'consistent selection: gold carriers leave more offspring, in every bag'. Two question marks hover, one over the triangle, one over the spread bracket.
scenes.narration: Last, let gold carriers leave slightly more offspring, in every bag. That is consistent selection. What happens to the triangle? And what happens to the spread?

scenes.visual: Freeze on the question marks. Small on-screen timer counts down 5 seconds; caption 'Predict: triangle? spread?'.

scenes.tts: The triangle creeps toward gold, so consistent selection pushes the average. But while both alleles remain, the dots keep scattering around it.
scenes.visual: Counter ticks 0 to 20 (computed, weak selection). The WHITE TRIANGLE trends right toward 1 while wobbling; the dot cloud moves with it but stays wide, with some dots still falling to 0 and stopping there. Label 'selection pushes the average; drift still spreads'.
scenes.narration: The triangle creeps toward gold, so consistent selection pushes the average. But while both alleles remain, the dots keep scattering around it.

scenes.tts: Here is the test. Compare the replicate average with what chance alone would give. Then, for selection, check whether carriers really do better. For gene flow, track the migrants.
scenes.visual: Three small panels side by side, each a dot cloud with its triangle: 'drift' (triangle at start, wide cloud), 'gene flow' (triangle shifted to immigrants), 'selection' (triangle shifted toward gold). Under them three stamps appear in turn: 'neutral null: what chance alone gives', 'fitness assay: do carriers do better?' and 'immigration and ancestry: who came in?'.
scenes.narration: Here is the test. Compare the replicate average with what chance alone would give. Then, for selection, check whether carriers really do better. For gene flow, track the migrants.

scenes.tts: One population's frequency, on its own, cannot tell luck from cause. Replicates give it an average to compare with.
scenes.visual: The three panels shrink away leaving a single dot alone on the axis with no triangle; a label 'one population: no average to compare' and a grey question mark. Then the 40-dot cloud fades back in around it with its triangle.
scenes.narration: One population's frequency, on its own, cannot tell luck from cause. Replicates give it an average to compare with.

scenes.visual: Hex end card. Take-home line: 'Drift spreads replicates; gene flow and consistent selection push their average.'
